statement: Let row_count(i) be the number of j with 0 <= j < len(bank[i]) and bank[i][j] = 49. Let i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k be exactly the row indices with row_count(i_t) > 0. The function returns a result r and: if k <= 1 then r = 0; if k >= 2 then r = sum_{t=1}^{k-1} row_count(i_t) * row_count(i_{t+1}).
preconditions: Let m = len(bank). Assume 1 <= m <= 500; there is an integer n with 1 <= n <= 500 such that len(bank[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, bank[i][j] is either 48 (ASCII '0') or 49 (ASCII '1').

statement: For every bank satisfying the preconditions, number_of_beams returns a result r (an Ok value); it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.

statement: Whenever number_of_beams bank returns r and number_of_beams bank' returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let m = len(bank). Assume 1 <= m <= 500; there is an integer n with 1 <= n <= 500 such that len(bank[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, bank[i][j] is either 48 (ASCII '0') or 49 (ASCII '1'). Let bank' be the row-reversal of bank: len(bank') = m, len(bank'[i]) = n for every i, and bank'[i][j] = bank[m-1-i][j] for every i,j.

statement: Define row_count_bank(i) as the number of j with bank[i][j] = 49, and row_count_bank'(i) as the number of j with bank'[i][j] = 49. If row_count_bank(i) = row_count_bank'(i) for every i with 0 <= i < m, then whenever number_of_beams bank returns r and number_of_beams bank' returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let m = len(bank). Assume 1 <= m <= 500; there is an integer n with 1 <= n <= 500 such that len(bank[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < m; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, bank[i][j] is either 48 (ASCII '0') or 49 (ASCII '1'). Let bank' be any other input satisfying the same constraints and having len(bank') = m.

Whenever number_of_beams returns a result r with r > 0, there exist indices i < j and columns c,d such that 0 <= c < len(bank[i]), 0 <= d < len(bank[j]), bank[i][c] = 49, bank[j][d] = 49, and row_count(k) = 0 for every k with i < k < j.

statement: Let row_count(i) be the number of j with 0 <= j < len(bank[i]) and bank[i][j] = 49. Whenever number_of_beams returns a result r, for every i < j with row_count(i) > 0 and row_count(j) > 0, if there exists k with i < k < j and row_count(k) > 0, then no laser beam has one endpoint in row i and one endpoint in row j; equivalently, the ordered row pair (i,j) contributes 0 to r.
